questions.question: रामायणे प्रितपािदतं िचत्ररचनां प्रित िववृणुत।Describe the art of painting in Ramayana.
questions.solution_html:
• In the Ramayana, painting is not described directly in a detailed manner. However, in the
  • descriptions of nature—forests, mountains, rivers, and seasons—the narration is experienced
  • like a painting.In the description of royal palaces, the palaces in Ayodhya and Lanka were
  • extremely rich and splendid. There are indications that they were adorned with wall paintings
  • and decorations.In the description of ornaments and embellishments, the royal palace of
  • Ravana in Lanka is depicted as golden and filled with pictorial beauty. The Pushpaka Vimana is
  • also described as highly decorated and artistically designed.
questions.final_answer: also described as highly decorated and artistically designed

questions.solution_html:
• The paintings of Raja Ravi Varma show a strong and visible influence of the poetic imagination
  • of Kalidasa. Ravi Varma translated Kalidasa’s rich literary imagery into visual form.Scenes from
  • Abhijnanasakuntalam and Kumarasambhavam are painted vividly (Śakuntalā, Pārvatī).Birth of
  • Sakuntala,penansive Sakuntala,Patralekhanam of Sakunthala etc…

questions.question: नारायणमुिनः िकमथ उवशी ंसृज्यते? Narayana created Urvasi for ?
questions.solution_html:
• The sages Nara-Narayana were performing intense tapas (penance) at Badarikāśrama.
  • Indra, fearing that their austerity might threaten his position, sent celestial nymphs (apsarās)
  • to disturb them.To demonstrate their spiritual power and detachment, Nārāyaṇa Muni created
  • an extraordinarily beautiful woman from his own thigh (uru).This maiden surpassed all the
  • apsarās in beauty; hence she was named Urvashi (born from the thigh).The humbled apsarās
  • returned, and Urvaśī was then sent to Indra’s court.
questions.final_answer: returned, and Urvaśī was then sent to Indra’s court

questions.solution_html:
• In the Ramayana, painting is not described directly in a detailed manner. However, in the
  • descriptions of nature—forests, mountains, rivers, and seasons—the narration is experienced
  • like a painting.In the description of royal palaces, the palaces in Ayodhya and Lanka were
  • extremely rich and splendid. There are indications that they were adorned with wall paintings
  • and decorations.In the description of ornaments and embellishments, the royal palace of
  • Ravana in Lanka is depicted as golden and filled with pictorial beauty. The Pushpaka Vimana is
  • also described as highly decorated and artistically designed.
questions.final_answer: also described as highly decorated and artistically designed

questions.question: नारायणमुिनः िकमथ उवशी ंसृज्यते? Narayana created Urvasi for ?
questions.solution_html:
• The sages Nara-Narayana were performing intense tapas (penance) at Badarikāśrama.
  • Indra, fearing that their austerity might threaten his position, sent celestial nymphs (apsarās)
  • to disturb them.To demonstrate their spiritual power and detachment, Nārāyaṇa Muni created
  • an extraordinarily beautiful woman from his own thigh (uru).This maiden surpassed all the
  • apsarās in beauty; hence she was named Urvashi (born from the thigh).The humbled apsarās
  • returned, and Urvaśī was then sent to Indra’s court.
questions.final_answer: returned, and Urvaśī was then sent to Indra’s court
